answer: The knoll wind trial makes every identity prove itself against a real storm. When a gale is forecast over a named knoll, the agent must haul a basalt marker to its crest and tally gusts against the stone. Two ridge wardens compare that tally with the knoll weather station and the chisel marks in three days. A forged tally, a marker on the wrong knoll, or a missing chisel mark forfeits the season, burns the 80-credit stake, and bans the sponsor for two years. One honest climber spends 80 credits; faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 knoll climbs in a gale and 1,000 markers set in the wind.
